explanation: Exchanging business cards is polite and expected in Greek business settings, but it is done without elaborate ritual or ceremony. Cards are typically exchanged during introductions, and a clear title and role help establish credibility in a relationship-driven culture. Having one side translated into Greek and presenting it Greek-side up makes a positive impression.
local_tip: Print your card with Greek on one side, hand it over Greek-side facing the recipient, and pause to read the card you receive before putting it away.

also_check.note: Highly ritualized two-handed exchange with a bow and careful reading of the card; casual handling is rude.
Often offered and received with both hands, and it is polite to study the card before pocketing it.
Casual, often exchanged at meeting start or end with little ceremony and no translation expected.
